sections.html:
This beautiful cichlid has been kept in the world's aquariums since 1906 and has delighted generations with its varied behavior and attractive brood care. The animals are typical open breeders with a parent family, i.e. both parents lead the numerous brood.

The maximum length of the fish is about 17 cm. They are able to spawn from a length of about 6-8 cm.
Andinoacara latifrons has always been considered a relatively calm, little burrowing species that is gentle with plants. The larger the aquarium, the more peaceful the cichlids are.

Confusion arose over time due to naming. For a long time the fish was listed in the genus Aequidens, and Andinoacara latifrons was long considered a synonym of the similar species A. pulcher. The animals described here are German offspring descended from parent fish caught in the Rio Atrato in Colombia.
